nodes.name: Verify JWT
nodes.notes: Public webhook branch only. 401 arrives as data (onError = continueRegularOutput).

nodes.name: Fetch HOT Leads from Supabase
nodes.notes: Replaced 30 Aug 2026. Was the Supabase node with returnAll:true and a single status=HOT filter, so EVERY hot lead ever recorded was re-pushed on every invocation -- unbounded memory on a 958 MB box and, before the identity fix, one fresh Bitrix duplicate per lead per run. Now PostgREST: same HOT filter, plus a crm_synced_at watermark (never synced, or last synced more than 6 h ago), newest first, hard limit 100. The limit is a Bitrix rate-limit budget, not a memory one: 100 leads x up to 3 REST calls at Bitrix's ~2 req/s is ~150 s, inside the 300 s executionTimeout. Written as an HTTP node because the Supabase node ANDs its filters and cannot express or=().

nodes.name: Find Lead by Email

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ entity_type: 'LEAD', type: 'EMAIL', values: [ $('Map Lead to Bitrix24 Lead').item.json._lead_real_email || '__nexus_no_email__' ] }) }}

nodes.notes: Second identity probe, and only ever a fallback. Runs against the REAL email only: the synthetic '+<digits>@whatsapp.lead' address is deliberately replaced with a sentinel that matches nothing, because asking Bitrix about an address no human ever typed is what produced the '__none__' lookup this fix removes. Unconditionally on the path so that $('Find Lead by Email') can never throw in 'Decide Update or Create' or 'Delivery Report'.

nodes.name: Safe to Create?
nodes.notes: TRUE = both duplicate probes answered, they agreed the customer is not in Bitrix, and the lead carries an identity we can match on next time -- so a create cannot duplicate anything. FALSE = we do not know, and a create would be a guess; the run writes an honest FAILED audit row instead and leaves crm_synced_at unstamped so the next invocation retries.

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Bitrix Lead
nodes.notes: Read-before-write. crm.lead.update overwrites whatever you send it, so the only way to keep a rep's handwritten COMMENTS is to read the field first and merge. Also yields DATE_MODIFY (has a human touched this record since our last push?) and the current OPPORTUNITY (is there already a negotiated figure we must not flatten?). If this read fails, NOTHING is written.

nodes.name: Build Update Payload
nodes.notes: The field-ownership rule lives here. COMMENTS is append-only around a delimited NEXUS block; OPPORTUNITY is fill-if-empty and is skipped entirely when Bitrix's DATE_MODIFY is newer than our own crm_synced_at; TITLE, NAME, PHONE, EMAIL and SOURCE_DESCRIPTION are never sent on an update at all.

nodes.name: Update Has Payload?
nodes.notes: TRUE = there is at least one field this sync is entitled to write. FALSE = either nothing changed (healthy no-op) or the read-before-write failed (refuse to write blind). Either way crm.lead.update is never called with an empty fields object, which Bitrix rejects, and DATE_MODIFY is not churned.

nodes.name: Link Back to Supabase
nodes.notes: Writes the crosswalk that makes identity resolution cheap and durable: leads.bitrix_lead_id (so the next run needs no probe and still matches after the customer changes number) and leads.crm_synced_at (the watermark 'Fetch HOT Leads' filters on, and the timestamp 'Build Update Payload' compares against Bitrix DATE_MODIFY). Stamped ONLY on a SUCCESS verdict - on a failure the row stays unstamped so the next invocation retries it. When there is nothing to stamp the URL targets a sentinel email that matches zero rows, so the no-op is a 204 rather than a branch.
